title: What If You Read on a Screen in Bed Every Night?

scenes.text: What if you read on a screen in bed every night? Your body would slip into jet lag.
scenes.keywords: person using tablet in bed dark

scenes.text: Harvard researchers had volunteers read for four hours before bed: five nights on an iPad, five on paper.
On the screen, the sleep hormone melatonin dropped by about half.
Its nightly rise came more than an hour and a half later, like jet lag every single evening.
They took longer to fall asleep, got less dreaming sleep, and woke up groggier.
Same story, same bedtime. The only difference was the glow.

description:
In a 2014 PNAS study by Brigham and Women's Hospital, 12 adults read for about four hours before bed on an iPad for five nights and from printed books for five nights.
With the light-emitting screen, evening melatonin was suppressed by about half, its timing was delayed by more than 1.5 hours, they took longer to fall asleep, had less REM sleep and were less alert the next morning.
